notes:
Top-line: small engineering platform company building a GitHub-style PR assistant plugin for enterprises. They want low-latency streaming in the IDE + high-quality diff summaries and auto-comment suggestions.

Discovery / timeline: 
- 2025-01-15: inbound demo request via website form (interested in reducing reviewer time).
- 2025-01-22: demo w/ Maya (AE) + Aaron (SE). Fireflies: ff_2025-01-22_pr-insight-demo-9812 (highlights attached).
- 2025-01-29: security kickoff call; supplied SOC2 cert and basic infra questions; asked for KMS/HSM options.
- 2025-02-05: architecture sync — they shared their GitHub App design and streaming plugin prototype.
- 2025-02-18: POC kickoff planning meeting; agreed success criteria and dataset for eval.

Use-case & requirements (from Aaron notes):
- Primary workload: PR review assistant across large mono-repo + many microrepos.
- Features needed: diff summarization (TL;DR + changelog), auto-comment generation (inline), candidate-ranking for comments, reranking of suggested fixes, and ability to surface related docs from internal wiki.
- Latency SLOs: interactive IDE streaming target <= 50ms RTT for first-token and sustained low streaming latency for subsequent tokens.
- Throughput: ~200 concurrent active devs during peak (CI-driven review windows).
- Model/versioning: must support per-org model pinning (stable model for prod, canary for beta), rollback on regressions.
- Caching/batching: expect heavy reuse of similar diffs; want autosuggest cache + prefix KV cache to reduce token costs.
- Integrations: GitHub App, Slack notifications, internal SSO (Okta), and ability to store embeddings for reranking in customer-managed storage.

Security / compliance notes:
- Require SSO/SAML (Okta), audit logs tied to user IDs, encryption-at-rest via KMS, and data residency for EU customers. Asked specifically: "Can we keep embeddings and audit logs in our VPC?"
- Concern about retention controls: legal wants ability to purge specific dev sessions on request.

POC scope & success criteria (agreed):
- Deliver a streaming-capable plugin (VSCode) demo with Redwood hosted endpoint and model pinning for two models (stable + fast-quantized).
- Provide metric sheet: median first-token latency, tokens/sec, error rate, and per-comment quality score via annotated sample set.
- Quality bar: summaries should be rated >= 4/5 by internal reviewers on 100 sample PRs; generated comments should be relevant and avoid hallucinations.

Technical blockers & open questions:
- IDE streaming: need guidance on socket strategy, SSE vs WebRTC vs SDK streaming; dev team prefers WebRTC for reliability behind corp proxies.
- Fallbacks: want automated fallback from large model -> quantized low-cost variant with graceful degradation of comment verbosity.
- Billing model: engineering wants predictable monthly committed spend (Dedicated) vs pay-as-you-go for initial POC.

Sales notes / quotes: 
- CTO (Anna Leigh): "We won't ship until the feedback loop in the IDE feels instant. If you can hit the latency + comment quality, we will consider dedicated capacity."
- Head of Platform: "Pinning models per-repo and rolling back quickly is non-negotiable."

Next steps (short):
- (Aaron) send POC plan + pricing options (hosted + dedicated) by 2025-02-24.
- (Maya) schedule engineering deep-dive re: SAML attributes for 2025-02-26.
- (Customer) deliver 100 PR samples + labeling rubric by 2025-03-03.

Stubs / links: Drive deck: /drive/PR_Insight/Redwood_pr_tech_deck_v2.pdf; Jira ticket INF-3241 created for streaming reliability questions.

Notes style: fragmented, action-oriented. Expect follow-ups on latency test harness and quantization profile suggestions from Optimize team.
